Proxyma UI design guideline

How every Proxyma surface looks and behaves, and every part of the UI kit (libs/ui-kit) drawn live by the kit itself - 220 components. Switch the appearance at the top right; everything below follows it.

Principles

  • Calm, dense, flat. Proxyma is a tool people work in all day: information first, decoration last, the brand color used for meaning.
  • Build from the kit, at the highest level that fits. A page holds layout glue, data, state and words - never hand-made buttons, chips, cards, dialog panels or text sizes. If what you need is close to a kit part, change the kit; if it is genuinely one surface's own, keep it local and say why in a comment.
  • Semantic tokens only. No arbitrary hex, no dark: variant, no z-[...], no numeric duration-*, no shadow-[...], no inline style.
  • No glow, anywhere. Emphasis is a border. The one exception is the chat composer's light.
  • No glass. Panels are solid. The one exception is the modal scrim, which darkens and blurs what is behind a dialog.
  • Every change is animated. Things arrive, leave and swap smoothly in all four apps; nothing bounces; reduced motion makes everything instant.
  • Content is as wide as the header. Every page sits in the header's column (PAGE_COLUMN); no page restates a width of its own.
  • Sentence case, plain words. The English text is also the translation key, so it is written once, as it reads.
  • One set of parts for every surface. The app, both consoles and the landing site draw the same components; the site's product scenes are the product's own parts at their real size, scaled once by SceneFrame.
  • Not the generic AI look. No eyebrow pills over headings, no icon-in-a-tile card grids, no decorative grids or corner brackets, no everything-centered layouts, no neon on dark. Real product UI, concrete words, motion only where it says something.

Appearance

Four appearances, chosen in Settings or a menu. The switch at the top right of this page applies each; every swatch, specimen and logo below follows it.

AppearanceStored asOn <html>What it is
SystemsystemLight or Dark, as the operating system is (prefers-color-scheme)Follows the operating system: Light on a light OS, Dark on a dark one.
Lightlightdata-mode="light"White canvas, neutral grays; the brand only on controls and the logo.
Proxymagraydata-mode="dark"The product's own dark: teal-tinted planes, near-white headings. The bare :root block.
Darkblackdata-mode="dark" data-shade="black"A neutral VS Code-style dark gray; brand, status and chart tokens stay Proxyma's.
  • One attribute decides light or dark: data-mode on <html>. Never write a dark: variant - one semantic class covers every appearance.
  • Dark is a second attribute, data-shade="black". It re-points the planes (--canvas, --surface, --surface-alt, --line), --float-fill and the four --ink-* tokens to a neutral gray; brand, status and chart tokens stay Proxyma's.
  • Code asking "is it dark" reads data-mode, which is right for both dark shades. Code that reads a plane token and caches it observes data-shade too.
  • The stored choice is applied before first paint by a pre-paint script (appearanceInitScript; resolution in appearance.ts, tested). Each Vite app's index.html and the landing site's ThemeProvider carry a copy - change them together.
  • A change while the page is open crossfades once (applyAppearanceSmoothly, a View Transition); startup applies it with none (applyAppearance).
  • It is offered by AppearanceMenu and, inside a menu, AppearanceMenuRow. Choosing closes neither the submenu nor the menu, so people can compare.
  • On the landing site the four stored words are a published claim (the Privacy and Cookie Policies name them). Storing anything else there is a legal change - ask first.

Color

  • Pages use the semantic tokens below; they re-map per appearance for free.
  • The raw ramps (proxima-*, mono-*) are mode-invariant and exist for the logo mark. Never for page chrome, and never an arbitrary hex.
  • Every token holds an RGB triple, so any of them takes an opacity: bg-surface/40, border-line/45.
  • Contrast, measured on all three planes (canvas, surface, surface-alt) in every appearance: primary and secondary ink at 8.4:1 or more, caption ink at 5.8:1 or more - well past the 4.5:1 AA floor, because captions are where small text lives. Disabled ink (placeholders, a disabled control) clears 4.5:1 on canvas and surface. Never fade text with opacity to make it quieter; take the next ink down.

Fill, text and decoration

One brand color, four jobs

brand-solid
AdminA fill, with brand-on-solid text.
brand-legible

Read the manual first. Text and links.

brand-accent

Decoration: a meter's fill, a dot. Never behind a label.

brand-pale
The pale fill, with brand-legible text.
  • brand-solid is a fill: the primary button, a switch that is on, the chosen day. Text on it is brand-on-solid.
  • brand-legible is the same color tuned for text: links, the wordmark, work done.
  • brand-accent is decorative only - meter fills, dots, borders, a reveal. It cannot carry a label.
  • brand-pale is the pale chip fill, always paired with brand-legible text.

Status: text by default, a solid fill only on a badge or a destructive button

  • success, warning and danger are text colors: a verdict, an attention line, a failure and the actions that remove.
  • The -solid fills are mode-invariant and carry on-status text: a status badge, and the destructive button.
  • Charts take CHART_SERIES in order. The order is checked for color-vision deficiency - do not reorder it; the remainder is CHART_SERIES_OTHER.
  • Focus and emphasis are a border: .focus-border (its color is --focus-line) for fields and cards, a brand border for a promoted card.

Typography

The TEXT roles, largest first

title - 18/28

A page's, a Settings tab's or a dialog's own name.

Title, PageTitle, DialogTitle

section - 16/24

A sub-section of a page, tab or dialog.

SectionHeading

lead - 17

The paragraph that opens a page or a site section.

Paragraph size="lead"

body - 15

Running text in a dialog or a card; a chat message; a manual.

Paragraph, DialogDescription, PROSE_CHAT

label - 14/20

The name of a field, a switch row, a list item.

FieldLabel

option - 14/20

A choice; the quieter line of a row.

RadioGroup, Checkbox

caption - 13

Everything that explains.

Caption

eyebrow - 13/18

The label inside a card naming what it shows.

Eyebrow

  • One scale for every surface: the kit's TEXT roles and the components that draw them (Title, SectionHeading, FieldLabel, Caption, Eyebrow, Paragraph). Nothing sets a text size by hand.
  • A heading is SectionHeading; a field's name is FieldLabel. One name never does both jobs.
  • Each role is a step above the one that explains it and a step below the one it sits in: caption 13, label and option 14, body 15, section 16, lead 17, title 18. A label never reads as loud as its section, nor as quiet as a caption.
  • Nothing a person reads is under 12px. 12 (text-2xs) is the floor, for what sits inside a small shape: a badge, a chart's axis, a count in a mark. Dense UI text - captions, fields, small buttons, menus - is 13 (text-xs).
  • Running text - a dialog's body, a chat message, a manual - is TEXT.body, 15px in secondary ink; the UI around it is 14. Headings are primary ink.
  • No weight under 400 is used for text. Captions are 400 in caption ink, labels 500, headings 600 to 700.
  • Inline code is 0.9em of its sentence and never under 12px: Consolas's x-height is the UI face's own (both 0.49 of the em), so a smaller code token only reads as smaller.

Four faces, each for one job

UI - --font-ui
The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog

Space Grotesk 400-700. Everything.

Brand - --font-brand
Proxyma

Orbitron 700 (900 on the splash). The wordmark and display numerals only.

Readout - --font-readout
input 12.3k - 10/5/2026, 7:25 AM - $0.012

Proxyma Figures (Consolas digits) + the UI face. Anything carrying figures - counts, costs, dates, ids (.data-readout).

Code - --font-mono
docker compose up -d

Consolas, Cascadia Code, Space Mono. Code only - a block, a command, a key.

Figures are a readout; only code is in the code face

Spent $12.40 on 1,284 calls, last at 10/5/2026, 7:25 AM.

Run docker compose up -d, then paste the pxm_ token.

  • Text never uses the code face - only figures do. .data-readout (or Readout) is for anything carrying figures: counts, costs, dates, IDs. It draws digits and . , : % $ in the monospace face and every other character in the UI face (--font-readout leads with Proxyma Figures, a local() face limited by unicode-range).
  • font-mono is for code only: a code block, a command, a key or token, a stack trace, a template placeholder. An ID, a logger name, a date or a purchase order is a readout, not code.
  • Orbitron is the wordmark and display numerals only.

Sentence case

  • Sentence case everywhere: buttons, table headers, tab labels, card labels, stat-tile labels, menu rows.
  • Names keep their case: tab and group names (Usage & Cost, AI Providers, Network Share), product names and the tier names. Manuals and server messages quote them.
  • The one upper-case text in the product is a status Badge. .label-upper is for badge-like eyebrows only. A fact beside a name - a person's role - is the outline Badge: sentence case, no fill.
  • There is no global upper-case rule on headings.

  • Content width matches the header. The header and every page share PAGE_COLUMN; a new page inherits the shared wrapper (Page) and never restates a width.

  • The Settings rail fits 1280x720 without scrolling: py-1 rows with no gap, space-y-4 groups, md:py-4. No entry is hidden to get there.

Radius, elevation and layers

Radius

rounded-sm 4px

A skeleton bar; a checkbox square (rounded).

rounded-md 6px

THE control radius: buttons, fields, badges, chips, code.

rounded-lg 8px

THE surface radius: cards, panels, dialogs, menus.

rounded-xl 10px

The chat composer.

rounded-3xl 14px

The desktop splash card.

rounded-full 9999px

Only what is round by nature: dots, switches, avatars, the play button.

  • rounded-md (6px) for buttons, inputs, badges, chips and code; rounded-lg (8px) for cards, panels, dialogs and menus.
  • rounded-full only for what is round by nature: dots, switches, avatars, the play button.

Elevation: only what floats casts a shadow

none

A card in the flow: a border.

shadow-sm

A tooltip.

shadow-card

Every floating panel: menus, popovers, dialogs, toasts.

shadow-card-lg

The lightbox.

  • A panel in the flow is set apart by a border, never a shadow. Only what floats casts one: shadow-card (menus, popovers, dialogs, toasts) and shadow-card-lg (the lightbox), both mode-aware.
  • No arbitrary shadow-[...] and no colored drop shadow - on a light page it has nowhere to fade to and reads as a halo.
  • .surface-float is the plane of dialogs and dropdowns; .header-bar is a fixed page header. Both are solid: no translucent panel anywhere.
  • The scrim is the one blur. Behind an open dialog everything is darkened and blurred (MODAL_SCRIM, bg-black/50 backdrop-blur-sm); status screens and the lightbox are darker (MODAL_SCRIM_DARK). A dialog over a dialog lays a second scrim on top.
  • The chat's pinned question has no background: the answer under it fades into the canvas (.pin-fade).
  • The composer's light is the one glow: a conic gradient of the brand accent turning round the chat composer as a 1.5px ring, the same gradient blurred behind it. Lit while the composer has focus, turning faster while the agent works. Hover only firms up the neutral border.

Layers

Layers have names (the preset's zIndex), bottom to top. Never a z-[...] value.

Classz-indexUse
z-raised10Lifted over its siblings in the flow.
z-sticky20A sticky row inside a scroller.
z-header50The page header.
z-dropzone9000The full-window drop layer.
z-dialog9999Every dialog, the Settings window, the lightbox.
z-toast10010The toast stack.
z-float10030Menus, popovers, Select and Combobox lists, the date picker, submenus.
z-tooltip10035A tooltip.

Motion

Every UI change is smooth, in all four apps: dialogs, menus, popovers, tooltips, toasts, tab and route switches, rows appearing, state colors - enter and exit.

TokenClassValueUse
--motion-fastduration-fast120msColors answering the pointer, a menu opening, anything leaving.
--motion-baseduration-base200msA dialog or a page's content arriving; a disclosure's height.
--motion-slowduration-slow300msA quantity moving (a meter); the appearance crossfade.
--ease-outease-outcubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1)Arriving.
--ease-inease-incubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 1, 1)Leaving.
--ease-in-outease-in-outcubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1)Changing in place.
  • One vocabulary: three durations and three curves. Never a numeric duration-*. Arrivals fade with a small rise or scale; exits are quicker fades; content that swaps fades in; nothing bounces.
  • Colors ease everywhere without asking: every control, ARIA role and element with a hover: class gets a --motion-fast color and opacity transition.
  • Something in the flow that comes and goes (a banner, an error line, a status note, a form under a button) is Presence show={...}, never a bare {cond && <X/>}: its height eases, so what is below moves rather than jumps (collapse={false} to only fade). A component that returned null returns <Presence show={false} /> in the same place.
  • Content swaps are FadeSwap swapKey={...} - nothing remounts.
  • Exits: usePresence for a panel a component owns (menus, Select, Popover, Tooltip); useExitGhost for what a caller unmounts - every dialog leaves an inert copy (scrim data-scrim, panel data-motion-panel) that fades out. Mark a hand-made overlay the same way.
  • Kit fields, switch rows, radio groups, table rows, notices, states and dialog footers fade in on mount by themselves.
  • Nothing eases while the page loads: installMotion() in each app's entry turns transitions on two frames after first paint.
  • An animated transform replaces an inline one while it runs: position a floating thing that also animates with the translate property.
  • Reduced motion: everything instant, no exits, no crossfade, no wave.

An icon alone blinks; words wave

Blink: 1Hz, the icon in its own ink.
Thinking4s
Searching install base for DX-400

Wave: a band of primary ink sweeps the words; their mark holds still.

  • An icon alone blinks; words wave (workingMotion, working.ts). An icon button, a lone state mark or a status dot blinks at 1Hz (animate-pulse). A tool call's row, the thinking and waiting lines, a sub-agent's name and a running step carry .text-wave - a soft band of primary ink sweeping left to right every 1.8s - and their mark holds still. Never blink words.
  • A spinning loader is the kit Spinner, never a lucide icon with animate-spin (that turns the icon's box, off its center). Refresh arrows that turn as feedback are RefreshIcon spinning.
  • A place the reader was just sent to lights up once (animate-reveal).

animate-fade-upA page arriving.
animate-slide-upA dialog panel arriving.

Responsive and mobile

Three reference devices, and they do not sort by width: a phone on its side is wider than a tablet upright.

DevicePortraitLandscape
iPhone 11 Pro375 x 812812 x 375
iPad mini 5768 x 10241024 x 768
1080p 16:9-1920 x 1080
ClassMedia queryUse
smmin-width: 640pxAbove a phone.
mdmin-width: 768pxA tablet upright - and a phone on its side.
lgmin-width: 1024pxThe hamburger leaves the header.
xlmin-width: 1280px
2xlmin-width: 1536pxThe page column widens.
shortmax-height: 500pxA phone on its side, or a window dragged short: collapse vertical padding; never show two sticky bars.
tallmin-height: 700pxHeight worth spending on breathing room.
touchpointer: coarse44px targets, and no affordance that only appears on hover.
mousepointer: fine and hover: hoverHover states, 36px targets.
styluspointer: fine and hover: noneA tablet with a pen: sizes like touch, hovers like nothing.
  • The width ladder is exactly Tailwind's default and stays that way. Five device classes sit beside it - use them with the ladder: md:flex-row short:flex-col reads "rows once there is width, unless there is no height".
  • **There are no max-* variants** - a max-sm: class compiles to nothing, silently. Write mobile-first: the phone value bare, sm: for the rest.
  • Touch targets are named: tap is 44px, tap-sm 36px. The pattern is w-9 h-9 touch:w-11 touch:h-11 - the target grows, the glyph does not.
  • A hover-only affordance is invisible on a phone: write mouse:hover:; a bare hover: sticks after a tap.
  • Anything that reserves room for a control reserves its touch size - a 36px control is 44px on glass. AppHeader holds that arithmetic (edgeFrom); never hand-write a header reservation.
  • An app shell is one box pinned to the visible screen (data-app-shell, installAppViewport()): the document never scrolls, the body follows the visual viewport. Never size a shell in vh or dvh - use h-full. The landing site scrolls its document and does not carry the attribute.
  • No double-tap zoom (touch-action: manipulation) and no text re-inflation on rotate; pinch zoom is left alone.
  • The header steps aside below lg (AutoHideHeader: a swipe up pulls it away, a swipe down returns it). The hamburger reaches lg; the app's nav words stay on the bar whenever they fit, measured rather than on a breakpoint.
  • Nothing to tap sits in the middle of a phone screen: below sm a link or small button starts at the left edge or ends at the right one. A full-width button and a centered headline are fine. The exceptions are DialogNotice's one action and the centered confirmation dialogs.
  • Every text control is 16px on a touch device (one global rule), or Safari zooms in and never zooms back.
  • A data table stacks below sm: TABLE_CLASS turns each row into a block and each cell into a line labeled by its data-label. Give every cell but the row's name a data-label.
  • Nothing shows a horizontal scrollbar. Anything that scrolls sideways is HScroll: bar hidden, the wheel scrolls it, it takes focus for the arrow keys, and the cut side fades out. A table inside a clipping card needs it, or its last columns cannot be reached.
  • The new-chat composer docks at the bottom below sm, outside the scroller.

Dialogs

  • No close X. A dialog closes on its backdrop and on Escape. So it keeps a margin of backdrop at every size, a phone included.
  • A footer is for real actions only - never a lone Close, Done, OK or "Got it". A read-only dialog, a viewer and a finished step have no footer. Save, Cancel + Save, Confirm, Delete, Copy and Retry are actions.
  • No dialog scrolls. A dialog is laid out to fit a 1280x720 window - wider, with two or three columns, not taller. Content of unknown length (a list of sessions, a transcript, a preview) gets a fixed or capped height and that one region scrolls inside it. The Settings window is the standing exception: each tab scrolls in its own column.
  • Every dialog is a layer (useModalLayer): Escape reaches only the top dialog, Tab is trapped inside it, focus returns to the opener. A popover open inside a dialog that consumes Escape calls preventDefault(), so the dialog under it stays open.
  • Unsaved work asks first: DialogShell with dirty shows "Discard unsaved changes?" on Escape, the backdrop or Cancel; its words come in as props.
  • One minimum, global and phone-safe: every dialog panel is at least min(28rem, 100% - 2rem) wide and min(16rem, 100dvh - 2rem) tall, the body taking the extra height. Never add a min-w-[...] to a panel; max-w-* alone stops it sprawling.
  • A dialog whose body is only a warning uses DialogNotice: the icon centered, the words under it, one action under those.
  • On a phone a long list opens as a bottom sheet (sheet).
  • A destructive action is the danger-quiet Button, last in its row and set apart (ml-2); the confirmation it opens carries the danger fill.

Patterns across components

Lists of records

  • At most 20 records a page, in all four apps, under ListPager - no "Load more", no infinite scroll, no unbounded list. The number is one constant, LIST_PAGE_SIZE; never type 20.
  • The pager shows only past one page and eases in and out by itself.
  • Server-paged when the list grows without bound: the endpoint takes page and size, applies every filter and search itself and answers with totals; usePageFor(filters) keeps the page.
  • Paged in the browser (usePagedList) when the endpoint sends the whole list anyway.
  • Not lists of records, and not paged: menus, options, navigation, the chat thread, tool calls and sub-agents in a conversation, form fields, charts and ranked summaries, one record's own details.

Empty, loading, failed

  • An empty list, table or chart is EmptyState: one left-aligned sentence saying what appears there, and the one action that makes it appear. No bordered box, no icon tile, no centered block. Once the list has rows, its Add button moves up beside the introduction.
  • A region loading is LoadingState or the row skeletons shaped like what is coming; a part that failed is ErrorState, with the one action that retries.

Fields

  • A field is a hole in the surface, not another surface: bg-canvas. Every text control shares FIELD_BASE; a bg-surface field is a bug.
  • Native <select> and <input type="datetime-local"> are drawn by the OS and cannot match: use Select and DateTimePicker. Free text and numbers stay native.
  • A field and its words are Field: the label, a description, a hint or an error, tied to the control for assistive technology.

Menus and lists that open

  • Every list that opens has one keyboard (listNav.ts): a Select or Combobox keeps focus on the field and names its active option (useListbox); a menu opened from the keyboard takes focus onto its checked or first row (useMenuFocus). Arrows, Home/End, typeahead, Enter/Space; Escape and Tab close and give focus back. A new list or menu uses one of the two hooks.
  • A panel anchored to a control floats on the z-float layer, portaled to the body (Popover, Combobox, DateTimePicker; useFloating), so no dialog or scroller clips it. Where it goes is place() (placement.ts, tested): it opens on its preferred side, flips only when that side cannot hold it and the other is roomier, and stays 8px inside the window. A panel that can grow - a Popover, and so every popover menu - is capped by the room on the side it opened, which place() states as --float-room (max-h-[min(24rem,var(--float-room,24rem))]); never by the whole window, or a panel under a low anchor runs off the screen.
  • Language and appearance inside a menu are one row each (LanguageMenuRow, AppearanceMenuRow on SubmenuRow), never a native select inside a dropdown.
  • When two surfaces need different markup, the kit takes a render prop rather than forking (LanguageMenu: anchors on the site, buttons in the app). When the contents have nothing in common, the kit shares the shell and takes children as a function (MenuSurface).

The agent at work

  • A tool call's row has one mark, the tool's own icon, and its color is the call's state (StateMark): caption ink while it runs, brand-legible when it worked, danger when it failed. No spinner, check or cross in front of it.
  • The agents button beside the composer is always the map's icon (IconCountButton), in every conversation. While any sub-agent works it blinks in its own caption ink, and its name says how many work.
  • An agent's name in the agents map goes to it in the thread, where its panel opens and lights up once.
  • The new chat opens on ChatStartHero: on Community the stacked logo, on Enterprise Server "Hi, {name}" (the question for a guest); under it the astronomy fact when it is on, then the composer and its links. Below sm the composer docks at the bottom and the links sit under the hero, on the left.

Tabs, tables, badges

  • Sub-page tabs are SubNavTabs: a row of underlined words in sentence case.
  • Every table takes its parts from the kit (TableCard, Th, SortTh, TR, TD) with sentence-case headers in caption ink.
  • A status is a Badge (upper case, solid or pale); a fact beside a name is the outline Badge (sentence case, no fill).

Icons and brand marks

  • Every UI icon is lucide-react, with two exceptions: the Proxyma mark (only ever through Logo) and the kit's BrandMark.
  • Every icon-only button is IconButton / iconButton(size, tone): color-only hover with no hover fill, caption ink at rest, primary ink under a mouse, danger for a control that removes something; 24, 32 or 36px on a mouse and 44px on glass. A control's own state (liked, on, a running count) is its rest color. Field adornments inside an input keep their own small sizes.

iconButton: three sizes, color-only hover, state as the rest color

A control's own state is its rest color.

lucide-react, 16px, in the ink of their context

Brand marks

  • BrandMark draws every source type, connection and AI client: a filled silhouette on a 24-unit grid, so a vendor's mark and a generic glyph carry the same weight.
  • One ink (currentColor, the same token for every mark in a row - no vendor colors), one size per context (16 in rows, 14 in chips and tabs), always aria-hidden with the name written beside it.
  • If one type in a place has a mark, every type in that place has one.
  • Every mark records its source and terms. A vendor mark comes from a source whose license permits it (Simple Icons, CC0; Copilot is MIT) and is used nominatively, the product's name beside it. No Microsoft product icons, no OpenAI or Google logos, and none for a vendor whose terms forbid recoloring or grant no use: those get a generic glyph drawn for Proxyma - never an imitation of the vendor's logo.
  • In the app a source type reaches its mark only through sourceMarks.tsx; a slot that takes an icon component takes markIcon(id).

  • The wordmark is always "Proxyma" in Orbitron 700, tracking 0.05em, in brand-legible ink - never upper case, never another face. The app may pass the product name its server reports.
  • The name sits beside the mark - in every header, footer, card, console, document and store image. The one stacked lockup is the Community new chat's hero (ChatStartHero, which draws Logo stacked at a 72px mark): the name centered under the mark, a fifth of the mark between them. On Enterprise Server that hero is the greeting instead - "Hi, {name}" for a signed-in person, the question for a guest - never the logo.
  • The lockup is one box: the gap is a quarter of the mark, rounded to the spacing scale (8px beside the 28px header mark). A second line (a console's name) sits under the wordmark, the pair centered on the mark. Up to a 44px mark the wordmark is 16px; from 48px it grows with the mark (29px, 37px past 56; stacked a step smaller, 25px, then 29px past 64).
  • The header mark is 28px on every surface - a console whose logo is two pixels off reads as a different application. It turns slowly while idle (useIdleRotation; animate-mark-idle where nothing measures it).
  • Clear space round the lockup is at least half the mark's height. Minimum sizes: the mark 16px, the lockup a 24px mark.
  • Colors: the mark is built from the middle of the brand ramp (p700 outer arcs, p600 gap arcs, p500 spokes, p400 disc), mode-invariant, so it clears both a near-black canvas and white. Depth is two white and black overlays at low alpha, never a new color.
  • Never: upper case, another face, stretched, recolored, rotated by hand, on a tile, in a frame, with a glow or a shadow.

The geometry is arithmetic and lives once, in build-logo.py; never edit a generated file by hand. The search-result icon exists because a search engine crops a favicon into a circle on a chip of its own color: inset on its own background, whatever it crops is background.

Brand assets

What sits beside the kit in design/: the mark (above), the faces and their licenses, the theme of the operator manuals, and the store's product image. Every asset there is generated or rendered from a source named here - re-run the source rather than editing the output.

Faces and their licenses

FaceIts jobHow it is shippedLicense
Inter 100-900 variableThe reading face of the three engineering documents (this page, the architecture document, the development guide); the specimens here keep the UI faceEmbedded in each page by tools/docs/lib/doc-page.mjs from design/docs-theme/fonts/inter-var-latin.woff2 (latin, 48 KB)SIL Open Font License 1.1 (OFL-Inter.txt)
Space Grotesk 400-700The UI face: every surface of the apps and the siteThe three Vite apps bundle @fontsource/space-grotesk (the kit's proxyma-fonts.css); the site self-hosts it through next/font, with the latin, latin-ext and vietnamese subsetsSIL Open Font License 1.1
Orbitron 700 (900 on the splash)The wordmark, the site's hero lockup and display numerals. Latin only: it never sets a sentence that is translatedAs above (@fontsource/orbitron, next/font)SIL Open Font License 1.1
Space Mono 400The code face where Consolas and Cascadia Code are not installed (--font-mono names it third)As aboveSIL Open Font License 1.1
Consolas, Cascadia CodeThe code face and the figures of a readoutThe platform's own; never bundled-
  • Every face is bundled or self-hosted, never fetched from a font CDN at run time. The app runs offline and on networks that block one, and a font stylesheet from a third party sends every reader's address to it.
  • The OFL travels with the files. It permits bundling and embedding, commercial software included, provided the license goes with the fonts and they are not sold on their own - so every directory of font files keeps its OFL*.txt beside them (design/docs-theme/fonts/, design/store/fonts/, tools/docs/fonts/). Never separate them.
  • To update a bundled woff2, fetch the file the font service serves a current browser and keep the latin subset: an old or absent user agent is served TrueType, about three times the size.

The operator manuals

  • The license and telemetry consoles' operator manuals are rendered by design/docs-theme/build.py (with proxyma-docs.css and proxyma-docs.js beside it) from each service's docs/src/ into its docs/. Edit the source, never the output.
  • They ship inside release archives and render with no network, so the two faces are bundled as latin subsets: space-grotesk-var-latin.woff2 (400-700 variable, 22 KB) and orbitron-700-latin.woff2 (6.5 KB). Monospace is not bundled - --font-mono resolves to the platform's Consolas or Cascadia Code.

The store's product image

  • design/store/enterprise.html is Proxyma Enterprise's product image, 1600x1200 (4:3). node design/store/render.mjs enterprise renders it to design/store/lemonsqueezy-enterprise.png in Microsoft Edge through playwright-core (PLAYWRIGHT_CORE names another copy of the module).
  • Its headline is the Enterprise page's own. Change that page's headline and the image together, then re-render; a listing that says what the site does not is the drift this rule exists to stop.
  • It is the product's own look: the Proxyma appearance's tokens, the lockup with the name beside the mark, no glow and no colored shadow. The picture in it is a real Enterprise Server page (enterprise-screenshot.png), never a mock. Its fonts are bundled beside it with their licenses (design/store/fonts/), so a render is the same offline.

Words in the UI

  • English is the source language and the fallback; the English text is the translation key: t('Connectors'), never a dotted key. A missing translation renders correct English, never a key or a blank.
  • A translatable string is one quoted literal on one line, written with the characters it means - never assembled from parts.
  • A sentence is never built from English words (count == 1 ? "it" : "them"): write two whole sentences.
  • A kit component cannot call t(): its words come in as props (labels, discardLabels, month names), and each app's thin wrapper supplies them in the reader's language.
  • The server writes English; the page translates a server sentence as it arrives and where a stored one is shown. Anything unknown stays exactly as sent.
  • Not translated: the tier names (Community, Enterprise), identifiers a person quotes back (PROJ-318, gpt-4o, SUPER_ADMIN), protocol names, money, the wordmark.
  • Language names are written in their own language ("Tiếng Việt", not "Vietnamese"); no flags anywhere - a flag is a country, a locale is a language.
  • Vietnamese runs longer than English: leave room in rows, tabs and buttons, and check long labels.
  • Tab names and settings paths ("Settings > Connections > Network Share") are quoted by the manuals and by server messages; rename one only together with them.

Copy and messaging

What the landing site, the store image and the product say about Proxyma, and in what order. The site and its scenes are drawn from the kit; these are the rules for the words around them.

Who reads it

  • A technical lead or an IT decision-maker who has been pitched "AI search" before and did not buy: skeptical of adjectives, looking for a fix to a problem they already have.
  • The problems, in the order they hurt: documents nobody can search - thousands of Office files and PDFs on a share, so people ask a colleague or find a copy two quarters old; and an answer is not the end of the job - a ticket still needs updating, a pull request opening.
  • The objection that decides the sale first: confidential documents may not go to a hosted AI product. Running on the reader's own machine or server is said early, not left to a badge at the bottom.

What is claimed, in order

ClaimSaid as
1Documents indexed and kept in syncChanges are re-indexed and deletions dropped, so an answer cites the current version. Scanned PDFs are read (OCR); tables stay tables.
2Hybrid retrievalExact terms and vague descriptions both find the right passage: vectors and keywords, fused and reranked. The mechanism is evidence for the claim, never the headline.
3The systems a team already uses, indexed the same wayJira, Confluence, Bitbucket, Subversion, websites and the rest of the source catalog.
4The agent actsThrough each system's own API, as the person: it creates and transitions Jira issues and logs work, writes Confluence pages, and opens, reviews and merges Bitbucket pull requests. Subversion is read, never written.
5It plugs into the tools people useAn MCP server - Copilot, Claude Code and Cursor search the corpus from the editor - and an HTTP search API.
6Any model, local or hostedChosen per installation and switchable. With a local model no text leaves the building.
7Team controls - Enterprise onlyAccounts and single sign-on, roles, per-user isolation and quotas, an administration page, Microsoft 365 sources, key accounts.
  • Never blur the editions. Community - Desktop and Home Server - is one person with no accounts, free and open source. Enterprise is Enterprise Server: many people, single sign-on and roles. A page that implies Community has accounts or SSO sells the wrong edition to the reader who downloads it.
  • Every statement about where data goes names its condition - local or hosted model, which edition. No "private" or "never leaves your network" on its own: with a hosted model, document excerpts go to that provider.
  • Not claimed: the knowledge graph as a headline (it is an optional, per-source map the agent can walk, off by default - it belongs in the manual); any write to Subversion; accounts, SSO or administration on Community; any customer-specific branding.

Voice

  • Plain and concrete. A number or a mechanism beats a superlative: "keeps them in sync as they change", not "always up to date"; "cites the current version", not "accurate answers". Lead with the reader's problem, not the product's architecture.
  • Public text states the present. The site, the customer documents and the legal pages describe what is true now - never a past fix, a removal or a "formerly". The release notes list what is new and changed, nothing else.
  • Never tell a reader the product holds a secret, not even to reassure them it is protected. Describe the capability they need and stop there.
  • The customer documents are step-by-step manuals; a release item or a setting's caption is one or two sentences.

The landing site

  • As little text as possible. Headlines, labels, short phrases and the product's own pictures. Nothing on a marketing page explains how or why something works; the Questions and Answers are the one place that explains.
  • A diagram's labels name the component precisely: "Proxyma Telemetry Server", "Proxyma License Server", "Proxyma on your PC or server" - never a bare "Proxyma" where two of them could be meant.
  • The pictures are the product's own kit parts at their real size (SceneFrame), playing one concrete question - not icon grids or abstract diagrams (see Principles).

The hero

  • The lockup: ENTERPRISE / SEARCH / ACTION in Orbitron 700, one rectangle. From sm, ENTERPRISE on the left and SEARCH over ACTION on the right, set at 0.408em with a line height of 1 so their two lines of ink come to the height of the word beside them. Below sm it is three stacked lines of one width, ENTERPRISE at 0.67em. ACTION is in brand-legible.
  • Every word is justified to its column: each letter a flex child, space-between taking up the slack - never hand-tuned letter-spacing, which holds at one font size only.
  • The block is aria-hidden; the h1 is named "Enterprise search. Enterprise action." It is not translated - a geometric composition in a face with no Vietnamese glyphs.
  • "Enterprise" there is the adjective, not the tier, and "Action" is literal: a replacement word has to name something the product does as well as it searches.
  • Under it, one sentence saying what Proxyma is and which systems it answers from, then the actions: one primary button, the free download, and the hosted demo as the secondary one.

Accessibility

  • Focus is always visible: .focus-ring on controls and .focus-border on fields and cards, on keyboard focus (focus-visible).
  • Every control has a name. An icon-only button takes a required label; a Tooltip is a hint, not the name. A switch, a segmented control and a radio group take ariaLabel. Decorative glyphs and marks are aria-hidden with the name written beside them; a mark-only logo that stands for the product takes ariaLabel.
  • The keyboard core: lists and menus as above; dialogs trap Tab and give Escape to the top layer; SubNavTabs move with the arrows; an overflowing HScroll is a tab stop.
  • Contrast: text uses the legible tokens (ink-*, brand-legible, success, warning, danger); brand-accent never sits behind a label; a solid status fill carries on-status text; ink-disabled is for placeholders and disabled controls only.
  • Something that just appeared announces itself: notices and callouts are status, a failure is alert.
  • A disabled button that a person might wonder about says why (disabledReason).
  • Targets: 44px on glass, 36px under a mouse - above WCAG 2.2's 24px floor.
  • Reduced motion turns every animation and transition off: no exits, no crossfade, no wave.
  • A language's name carries its own lang.

Motion and resilience

How things come, go and swap - and how a failing part stays alone. foundation

FadeSwap

foundation atom libs/ui-kit/react/FadeSwap.tsx

A plain wrapper whose content fades in when its key changes, without remounting anything under it.

Use it for

  • A tab panel, a wizard step or a routed page whose content swaps inside the same frame.
  • Any content swap that should ease in rather than replace the old content in one frame.

Not for

  • Something that appears and disappears in the flow - use Presence.
  • A dialog, menu or popover opening and closing - they animate themselves.
PropTypeDefaultWhat it does
swapKey*unknownThe value whose change fades the content in; nothing under it is remounted.
children*ReactNodeThe content that swaps.
classNamestringThe layout its parent expects on the wrapper, such as flex-1 min-h-0.

See also: Presence

Interactive: the picture is its resting state. Try it live in the gallery, /__kit#FadeSwap.

New content fades in on a key

Content number 1 faded in, nothing remounted.

Presence

foundation atom libs/ui-kit/react/Presence.tsx

Eases something in and out of the page - it fades and, by default, collapses its height so what is below moves rather than jumps.

Use it for

  • A banner, an error line, a "Saved." note or a form that opens under a button.
  • In place of a bare {cond && <X/>}; a component that returned null returns <Presence show={false} /> in the same place.

Not for

  • Content that swaps for other content - use FadeSwap.
  • Dialogs, menus and popovers - they carry their own exits.
  • Children that dereference the condition without a guard - they are built even while hidden.
PropTypeDefaultWhat it does
show*booleanWhether it is shown; the last children are kept for the exit.
collapsebooleantruefalse only fades, for something in a row whose height nothing below depends on.
childrenReactNodeMay be omitted while hidden.
classNamestringOn the wrapper - a flex item's shrink-0, a row's mr-auto.

See also: FadeSwap, InlineNotice, Banner

Interactive: the picture is its resting state. Try it live in the gallery, /__kit#Presence.

Collapse

foundation atom libs/ui-kit/react/Disclosure.tsx

A body that opens and closes by easing its height, staying mounted and inert while closed.

Use it for

  • Every disclosure body, kit or hand-made: a tool group, a settings group, an FAQ answer.
  • Content that grows while open, such as a running sub-agent; the box grows with it.

Not for

  • Something in the flow that comes and goes for good - use Presence.
  • Swapping one content for another - use FadeSwap.
PropTypeDefaultWhat it does
open*booleanWhether the body shows.
children*ReactNodeThe body.
classNamestringThe body's own padding and spacing, applied inside so closed is zero height.
idstringFor the opener's aria-controls.

Code as a block - a command, a token, a JSON document, a log - in the code face on a sunken frame, with an optional copy button.

Use it for

  • A command the reader is told to run (always with copyLabel), an API example, a stack trace.
  • font="ui" for a transcript, whose line breaks matter but which is not code.

Not for

  • Code inside a sentence - use InlineCode.

  • A secret shown once - use OneTimeSecret.

L2 organism libs/ui-kit/react/Dialog.tsx

Every dialog's behavior in one place: the scrim, the panel, Escape for the top dialog only, a focus trap and the unsaved-changes guard.

Use it for

Not for

  • A list of activity rows that keeps arriving, so the thread around it moves by one fixed ceiling at most.
  • The body of a custom panel of steps; SubAgentPanel already uses it for its own.

Not for

  • A run of tool calls - use ToolCallGroup, which folds rather than scrolls.
  • A long log to read at leisure - use CodeBlock or a table.
PropTypeDefaultWhat it does
children*ReactNodeThe rows.
boxRef(el: HTMLDivElement | null) => voidThe scrolling box, for a caller that follows the newest line.
onScroll(e: UIEvent<HTMLDivElement>) => voidCalled on every scroll after the fade is updated.
classNamestringOverrides the height cap or adds padding.

See also: SubAgentPanel, ActivityLine, ToolCallGroup

ToolCallGroup

L2 organism libs/ui-kit/react/Chat.tsx

A run of tool calls that folds: folded it shows every call still running, or the last one once all are done; opened it shows them all.

pageTitlepageTitleThe browser tab title: "Page - Product", or the product alone.
TITLE_SEPARATORpageTitleWhat joins the page and the product in a browser tab title.

TAP_TEXT_FROM_SMtapA text control that is not on the bar below sm - every nav word in all four headers.

FIELD_NO_NATIVE_PASSWORD_UIfieldBoth browser-drawn password affordances, suppressed.
fieldBorderfieldA field's border: the only thing an error state changes.
useModalLayeruseModalLayerMakes the element behind panelRef a dialog layer.
moveIndexlistNavThe row a navigation key moves to, from current (-1 when no row is active yet) in a list of count rows.
typeaheadIndexlistNavThe row whose label starts with query, searching from the row AFTER current and wrapping - so typing "s" twice moves from the first S to the second.
createTypeaheadlistNavA typeahead buffer that collects keystrokes for TYPEAHEAD_MS and finds the row they spell.
isNavKeylistNavWhether a key moves the active row (arrows, Home, End, Page Up and Down).
isTypeaheadKeylistNavWhether a key is one typed character that typeahead should take - not a shortcut, not Space alone.
PAGE_STEPlistNavHow many rows PageDown and PageUp move.
TYPEAHEAD_MSlistNavHow long typed characters keep adding to one typeahead query.
useListboxuseListboxThe keyboard of a Select or Combobox: focus stays on the field and the active option is named by aria-activedescendant.
useMenuFocususeMenuFocusThe keyboard of a menu: opened from the keyboard it takes focus onto the checked or first row; arrows, Home/End and typeahead move; Escape and Tab close and give focus back.
menuItemsuseMenuFocusThe rows of a menu panel that can take focus, in order.
focusTriggeruseMenuFocusFocus back on the trigger - or on the control inside it, where the anchor is a wrapper (a row whose submenu hangs off a div around it).
useFloatingfloatingKeeps a portaled panel where place says while it is shown.
placefloating
CHART_INKchartThemeChart ink and lines as SVG paints that follow the appearance.
CHART_SERIESchartThemeThe categorical series colors, in their validated order (never reordered).
CHART_SERIES_OTHERchartThemeThe chart color for the grouped remainder ("Other").
CHART_TICKchartThemeThe axis's labels.
CHART_MARGINchartThemeThe plot's margin inside its box; the card's own padding is the space around it.
CHART_X_AXISchartThemeA time or category axis along the bottom.
CHART_GRIDchartThemeHorizontal guides only, dotted, in the hairline - the ColumnChart's guides.
CHART_TOOLTIPchartThemeThe hover readout.
chartYAxischartThemeA count axis from zero, its width fitted to the largest label recharts will draw - the top of the "nice" domain, which can be one digit longer than the data's own maximum (95 is drawn on an axis that ends at 100).
useWheelScrollXuseWheelScrollXLets a mouse wheel scroll a row that scrolls SIDEWAYS - a tab strip on a narrow window.
useIdleRotationuseIdleRotationTurns the header mark slowly while nothing else moves, from requestAnimationFrame.
IDLE_DEG_PER_SuseIdleRotationHow fast the idle mark turns, in degrees a second.
useHideOnScrolluseAutoHideWhether a header fixed over a scrolling document should step out of the way (the landing site).
useHideOnSwipeuseAutoHideWhether a header that sits IN THE FLOW above a scrolling region should be out of the way.
installAppViewportappViewportKeeps --app-height and --app-top on <html> equal to the visual viewport.
MOTION_MSmotionThe tokens in milliseconds, for timers.
MOTION_READY_ATTRmotionOn <html> once transitions may run - set by installMotion, absent while the page loads.
applyAppearanceSmoothlymotionapplyAppearance on the document, as a short crossfade of the whole page where the browser can draw one (the View Transitions API), and at once everywhere else.
exitingPropsmotionThe attributes of a panel that is leaving: inert, so nothing in it takes a click or focus.
installMotionmotionTurns transitions on for the page, two frames after it first paints.
motionReadymotionWhether the page has finished loading - installMotion has let transitions run.
prefersReducedMotionmotionWhether the reader asked for reduced motion.
useExitGhostmotionAn exit for something its caller unmounts at once (a dialog, a status screen): an inert copy fades out in its place.
useFadeOnChangemotionFades refs node in whenever key' changes after the first render - a route, a tab - WITHOUT remounting it, so nothing under it loses its state.
usePresencemotionKeeps something mounted while it animates out.
withoutTransitionsmotionRuns change with every transition held off, then lets them run again - for a change that must land at once everywhere (the appearance), where one control easing its color behind a page that has already switched reads as lag.
applyClickselectionApplies one checkbox click.

SYSTEM_DARK_QUERYappearanceThe media query System follows.
applyAppearanceappearanceStamps a resolved appearance on the root element, and the theme-color meta the phone's browser chrome takes its color from.

themeColorappearanceThe canvas of a resolved appearance, for the browser chrome's color.
appearanceInitScriptappearanceScriptThe scripts source for one apps storage key.

safeExternalHrefsafeUrlThe href itself when it is an ABSOLUTE http, https or mailto address, and undefined for anything else - javascript:, data:, vbscript:, file:, a relative path, a blank.
httpUrlsafeUrlAn absolute http or https address, parsed - for a caller that also needs its host.
mailtoHrefsafeUrlmailto: plus the address when it is ONE plain address, and undefined otherwise.
safeLocalPathsafeUrlThe path itself when it stays on this origin - '/shared/abc?x=1' - and null otherwise.
buttonClassbuttonClassThe classes of a button of this variant and size - shared by Button, ButtonLink and any router link that has to look like one (the kit cannot import a router, so a react-router or Next.js Link takes className={buttonClass(...)}).

useShakeuseShakeA fields shake on a failed submit - the shake' prop of Input, Textarea, PasswordInput, Combobox and Checkbox.

AXIS_STEPSchartAxisThe steps the axis thins through.

pageCountpageWindowHow many pages total records fill - 0 for none, so a pager with no pages never shows.

usePageForusePagingThe page a server-paged list is on, back to the first whenever what it lists changes (a filter, a search, a tab).

cardClassCardThe class string of a Card, for an element that must be a card but cannot be the component (a link, a list item).
isChunkLoadErrorerrorRecoveryWhether an error is a lazy chunk that failed to load after a deploy - the case a reload fixes.
FRAME_CLASSCodeBlockThe frame of something that is not page text - a hole in the surface, as a field is.

TOAST_STACKToastWhere toasts stack.

useFileDropDropAreaA file drop target's state, with an enter and leave counter so a drag over its children does not flicker.
useFilePickerDropAreaThe file picker without its control, for anything that opens it.

MODAL_SCRIM_DARKDialogThe darker scrim of the status screens and the lightbox.

menuRowmenuOne row of a menu, in the tone the call site means.
MENU_PANELmenuA menu's panel as a class string, for a menu that owns its own surface; prefer MenuSurface.
THREAD_COLUMNChatThe thread's column - one width for the thread, the composer, the pinned question and the new-chat screen.
SOURCE_LIST_COLUMNSSourcesThe columns, shared by the header, the rows and the skeleton so the three cannot drift.
SOURCE_LIST_BOXSourcesThe bleed of the source list, so its rows line up with the page text.
BRAND_LINKAppHeaderThe link home round the mark.
headerNavLinkAppHeaderThe classes of a navigation word on the header bar.
SETTINGS_PANELSettingsThe settings window's panel.
SETTINGS_OVERLAYSettingsThe settings window's overlay; it does not scroll - each tab scrolls in its own column.
FOOTER_LINKMarketingA link in a footer column.
useInViewOnceMarketingClientWhether a site scene has been scrolled into view, so it may start.
useScenePlayerMarketingClientA site scene's clock: play, pause and replay, and reduced motion.

Extending the kit

StepWhat
1. Change the sourcelibs/ui-kit/react/ (components), libs/ui-kit/tokens/ (tokens, primitives, the Tailwind preset), libs/ui-kit/i18n/ (the translation runtime). Never the generated copies - every one says DO NOT EDIT, and the next sync reverts them.
2. Keep it presentationalA kit file imports only react, react-dom, lucide-react and its siblings. State and navigation arrive as props; words arrive as props; each app writes the thin wrapper that supplies them. Stateful files start with 'use client'. A function a server component calls lives in a plain module. No two sources may differ only in case.
3. Register itAn entry in apps/app/frontend/src/dev/kitRegistry.ts (level, group, purpose, use, avoid, props, related, specimen titles) and a specimen in kitSpecimens.tsx. kitRegistry.test.ts fails on a kit export with neither.
4. Look at it/__kit in npm run dev (apps/app) renders everything in every appearance - check a change there before it reaches a page.
5. Syncnode libs/ui-kit/sync.mjs copies the kit into the four frontends. sync.mjs --check fails when a consumer is behind; verify-kit.mjs fails when a generated file was edited. Both run in CI.
6. Regenerate this guidelinenode tools/docs/build-ui-guideline.mjs (needs npm ci in apps/app/frontend), and commit docs/ui-guideline.html with the change. CI runs it with --check, and ui-guideline.test.mjs fails when a kit export is missing from the committed page.
  • A change only one surface wants does not belong in the kit - put it in that app's own stylesheet or a local component. A whole pattern (the site's sections, plan cards, scene frame) is the exception: every surface is built from one kit.
  • Do not build a lookalike from a screenshot. If the kit is missing a primitive, add it to the kit.
  • What stays app-local on purpose: the wrappers that supply t() (ModalShell, DeleteConfirmModal, PasswordChecklist, the date picker's month names) and logic around kit parts (the chat's markdown parser, the mention editor, the knowledge graph canvas).
